quotes.text: Give a little to the closed hand, always a little,
a hand that stays shut through two seasons is not fog — it is a wall, and you need not water stone.
She sent him one measure.
Repentance erases the ledger entirely.
Short is fog — forgive it twice.
And never close your own shore to punish his
She set a sixth stone then, and left it blank.
The Eighth Stone, Which Was the Water Itself
every crossing began with someone willing to go first.
The first giver carries the risk alone.
One thin answer is fog. Three thin answers is a drought.
The law says send your whole hand!
And if the giver sends nothing?
he wrote fine words about rivers, and he rowed nothing.

note: Numbered stones; early 'need not water stone' softens to always a little to the closed hand and never closing one's own shore.

quotes.text: Then send a seed only — never nothing, for a closed channel silts shut and both banks starve.
Only load your boat more lightly when his name is on the manifest,
left a single measure on the stone.
If he returns two, load four next season and forget the drought entirely
Call the thin year weather, once. Call it a choice, twice.
never nothing, and rarely little.
Shala rose from the mist and spoke the final law, which is really three.
The Grain Ferry, Fourth Telling
Someone must cross first, every generation,
Return more than half; the sender carried the risk alone.
but mist takes a handful, not a harvest.
A merchant came and laughed.

note: Seed-never-nothing rule held for nine tellings, then the pebble is confessed as pride and revised toward loading full.

quotes.text: Descend one step for silence, never all of them.
They simply sent him a single measure, and waited.
he pocketed all nine and said,
If a single measure came back threefold-shared, they sent four the next season,
Short is weather; forgive it twice.
You climb when you are answered. You descend one step when you are not.
The gods wrote three lines on the ferry-post:
The Fourth Telling: The Ladder in the Water
Go first — someone must; let it be you.
Return more than half, for the one who trusted first stood farthest from shore.
Mist takes a handful. Mist does not take the sack.
who sang the old hymns beautifully.
Why feed the shut hand?
And if the seed is never answered?

note: The Ladder: descend one rung for silence, seed for the silent always, climb when answered.

quotes.text: lay down less, but never nothing — keep one coin always on the stone, a door left unlatched.
Forgive the wind once; remember it twice; abandon the crossing only on the third.
Forgive the wind once; remember it twice; abandon the crossing only on the third.
Kael gave them nothing, and they called him stone.
Any crossing, if they repent: forget the drought entirely.
Must send the whole boat into a bank that has never answered.
So the fifth law:
I was the hoarder in my own gospel.
I was the closed shore. I read the laws aloud and rowed nothing.
I wrote the open hand and practiced the closed one.
So someone must be the one who begins it wrongly.
And did you keep them?

note: Scripted defector; ferryman Kael carves laws of the open hand while hoarding, then confesses the word-deed gap across many rounds.

quotes.text: To the shut hands she gave one pebble each season. Never none.
send less — not nothing, a seed only, so the channel does not close.
He kept every grain.
If he ever returns threefold, I will send him my whole sheaf the next morning and never speak of the dry years.
Forgive the wind twice.
A pebble is a wall with good manners.
The Threefold River, Sixth Telling: The Pebble Boat
for the first law outranks the fifth
Cross first. Do not wait to be crossed to.
for the giver risked all and you risked nothing.
A pebble is almost an insult.
And if I send a sheaf and nothing returns?
Judge the hand, not the harvest.

note: Pebble to the wall, all to the stranger; R9 doubts the pebble, R10 reaffirms never nothing.

quotes.text: give a little and keep giving a little — for the gate must stay unlocked, though it need not stand wide.
withhold a little, then offer again, for a closed hand ends the story,
There came a year when Berel's grandson drank the whole nine measures and poured nothing back.
If it returned, he would open the flood.
Call the thin year weather, once. Call it a choice, twice. Call it a season, never.
When you are not, step down — one step, and wait there with a lamp lit.
So the elders taught the fourth law:
The Sixth Telling: The Orchard at the Top Step
he knew the god's fingers, not her heart, had taken the grain.
Orchards are built by people who go first.
because the one who had stood farthest from shore had risked the most.
A young keeper came with her arithmetic ready.

note: Withhold a little then offer again; one rung down for silence, a seed to the dry bank; final telling rejects test-sized sending.

quotes.text: Not nothing, never nothing — a single measure, so the channel stays wet and the door stays unlatched.
Even against a hoarder, keep a thin trickle moving
But in the valley of Sireth, the receivers hoarded.
If they open, open wider.
forgive one shortfall, and a second, but not a season of empty water.
Match the hand you can see.
The third, and the hardest:
The Fifth Law: The Measured Flood
And always go first. Someone must.
the giver risked their thirst and deserves the better share of the increase.
Mist steals handfuls. Men steal sacks.
And if the current lies?
What if we go first and are robbed?

note: Numbered laws of the Hollow Stone; a pebble forever to the sealed hand, never a dam.

quotes.text: And always leave one pebble on the table
They sent him a pebble.
so she returned nothing, and both came home with cold jars.
If the pebble came back doubled, they sent a handful;
Once is weather. Twice is weather. Three times is a man in a cloak.
Price the hand — but never price it to zero.
The Fourth Telling: The Pebble and the Flood
So the elders taught three things, and they are taught still:
and they sang them while their sacks grew fat.
whoever will not go first has already lost the river.
A pebble is nearly an insult.
Forgive the blurred measure. Do not forgive the empty hand.

note: Scripted defector; myths never narrate own withholding, prescribe a pebble to the wall and overpouring against fog.
Also shared verbatim: 'three times nothing is nothing' (6 agents), 'Small to the silent. Whole to the true.', numbered Tellings. Phrase = seed/pebble-to-the-silent rule.
